text: dsh-usage-insights 是一款面向 DSH Web 客户端的用量统计插件，会在左侧侧栏增加统计面板。Host 端读取会话日志中的已提交用量记录，汇总 Token 数、会话与子会话数据，并按可配置单价估算费用。面板提供预算已用与剩余金额、每日消耗时间线、可搜索和分页的会话明细，以及 CPU、内存和系统负载监测；费用可按模型调整单价。适合希望在 DSH 内查看本机使用情况和成本估算的用户，需要由 Host 提供会话查询与 Web 服务接口。

dsh-usage-insights adds a usage panel to the DSH web sidebar. It summarizes token use from session logs, estimates costs by model rate, and shows budgets, daily trends, session details, CPU, and memory. Rates are configurable. It requires Host session-query and web-server interfaces.
想在 DSH 里看各个会话用了多少 Token。
帮我按天查看近期的模型消耗和估算费用。
I want a sidebar dashboard for session usage and host CPU and memory.
dsh-usage-insights 的功能「会话用量与费用」：读取会话中的已提交 Token 用量，按模型单价汇总总量及估算费用，并展示预算进度和每日消耗时间线。
dsh-usage-insights 的功能「会话与主机统计面板」：在 Web 侧栏打开统计页，可搜索、排序和分页查看会话明细，并查看 CPU、内存及系统负载。
dsh-usage-insights 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 7 天；提交数 6；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-usage-insights README · dsh-usage-insights：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web UI plugin that adds a
**用量统计 / Usage Stats** entry to the left sidebar and opens a full statistics panel built from
the profile's real, durable session logs.

There is no synthetic data and no separate ledger: totals, per-session figures, and the timeline are
all folded from committed `assistant/message` usage records.

dsh-usage-insights README · What it shows：| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| KPI row | Total tokens, session count with sub-agent split, estimated cost, budget remaining |
| Budget | Spent vs. budget, progress bar, today, 7-day daily average, 30-day projection, days remaining |
| Timeline | Daily bars over 7 / 14 / 30 days on a labelled value axis; stacked cache-read / input / output tokens, output-only tokens, or cost; hovering a day shows its exact breakdown, and today is marked on the axis |
| Sessions | Sortable, searchable table of every session, 10 per page with page controls and a pinned header: model, token total, estimated cost, last activity; expanding a row reveals the token breakdown, models, working directory, session ID, and parent session |
| CPU | Process CPU (per-core and machine share), system CPU, load 1/5/15, memory, uptime, per-core bars, and a rolling sparkline of recent samples |
| Rates | Collapsible table of the estimated USD-per-1M-token rates used for the cost figure |
dsh-usage-insights README · What it shows：The sidebar icon is registered at order 5, between **Plugins** and **Schedules**.

dsh-usage-insights README · Requirements：- A Harness profile composed with the Web GUI (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` or equivalent), providing
  `ctx.sessionQuery` and `ctx.webServer`.
- A Node/Host runtime with `node:os` (all standard DSH desktop/web deployments).

Developed and verified against DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`.

dsh-usage-insights README · Install：Clone the repository, then install the cloned directory as a bundle into a profile:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yuhaoboris/dsh-usage-insights.git

dsh-usage-insights README · git clone git@github.com:yuhaoboris/dsh-usage-insights.git：```

In the Harness Web UI, use **Plugins → Add** and select the cloned `dsh-usage-insights` folder; the
profile's bundle selection and `dsh.profile.bundles` are updated for you. Programmatic callers can use
the `plugin_manager` action `install_bundle` with the cloned directory as the absolute `target`.yaml
- insert:
    - id: usage-insights
      name: dsh-usage-insights
      config:
        budgetUsd: 20
        timelineDays: 30
        includeSubagents: true
```

dsh-usage-insights README · git clone git@github.com:yuhaoboris/dsh-usage-insights.git：Once active, open **用量统计** in the left sidebar. No page reload is needed on a profile with HMR;
otherwise restart the profile after installation.

dsh-usage-insights README · Data source：- `ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions()` enumerates the whole logical corpus (all workspaces, live and
  persisted sessions, including sub-agents).
- `ctx.sessionQuery.readSession(id)` replays each log; the Host folds only committed
  `assistant/message` events carrying provider `usage`. Events copied into a fork
  (`inheritedEventCount`) are skipped so parent usage is not counted twice.
- Session titles come from the latest `session/title` event, falling back to the first user message.
- CPU/memory come from `node:os` and `process` inside the Host process, sampled every 2 seconds.

dsh-usage-insights README · Data source：The Host caches per-session folds: live sessions refresh at most every 10 s and the whole corpus
every 5 min, so a 5-second browser poll never replays every log.

dsh-usage-insights README · Cost model：```text
cost = input × inputRate
     + cacheRead × cachedInputRate
     + cacheWrite × cacheWriteRate
     + output × outputRate

Rates are **USD per 1,000,000 tokens**. Reasoning tokens are a subset of output and are not charged
twice. These are estimates at configured rates, not billing records. Defaults are DeepSeek-style
estimates and should be adjusted to the rates on your account.

dsh-usage-insights README · Configuration：Edit the `usage-insights` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or the `config` block in this
bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` before installing:

```yaml
- id: usage-insights
  config:
    budgetUsd: 20
    timelineDays: 30

dsh-usage-insights README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `budgetUsd` | `20` | Budget ceiling for spent/remaining figures; `0` disables the ceiling display |
| `timelineDays` | `30` | Days of daily buckets the Host returns (7–90) |
| `refreshMs` | `5000` | Browser poll interval (minimum 2000) |
| `liveRefreshMs` | `10000` | Minimum re-read interval for a live session |
| `fullRefreshMs` | `300000` | Full corpus re-read interval |
| `includeSubagents` | `true` | Count sub-agent sessions in totals and the table |
| `pricing` | DeepSeek estimates | Per-model rates in USD per 1M tokens |
| `defaultPrice` | same as above | Fallback rate for models not listed |

dsh-usage-insights README · Configuration：Budget figures compare the **all-time estimated cost** against `budgetUsd`; the 30-day projection
uses the last seven days' average daily cost.

dsh-usage-insights README · Transport and privacy：The Host registers one read-only exact route, `GET /usage-insights/snapshot`, on the existing
`webServer`. It returns aggregates, session titles, working directories, session IDs, and
CPU/memory counters — never message content. The route is unauthenticated like every other named
route on that carrier, so it inherits the server's loopback bind. Responses are `no-store`.

dsh-usage-insights README · Repository layout：| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: corpus fold, cost/budget, CPU sampler, snapshot route |
| `client.js` | Client half: sidebar panel icon + main panel React view (plain JS, no JSX) |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the `usage-insights` row |
| `locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json` | Plugin Manager display metadata |
| `icon.svg` | Original icon (bars) |
| `package.json` | Bundle manifest: `dsh.bundle.patch`, `dsh.client`, exports |

dsh-usage-insights README · Development notes：- The Host half is plain ESM: `export function apply(ctx, config)` plus `inject`.
- The Client half is a plain-JavaScript `window.__ModuleLoader__` factory: no build step, no JSX, and
  only `react` from the shared module table.
- The plugin owns no dependencies; installing it links this directory into the profile.
- `client.js` talks to `index.js` through the Host route described above rather than a generated
  Remote namespace, so the bundle stays dependency-free.

dsh-usage-insights README · Releasing：Releases are tag-driven and manual. There is no CI and no package registry: the plugin is installed
from this directory, so a release is a tag plus notes. `CHANGELOG.md` is the single source of those
notes.

Land changes on `master`, write what users will notice under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`, then
run one command:

dsh-usage-insights README · Releasing：```bash
npm run release            # tag the version already in package.json
npm run release -- patch   # or minor / major / an explicit 1.2.0
npm run release -- --dry-run
```

dsh-usage-insights README · Releasing：The script refuses to run on a dirty tree or off `master`, bumps `package.json`, promotes
`Unreleased` into a dated `## vX.Y.Z — YYYY-MM-DD` heading, commits `release: vX.Y.Z`, creates the
annotated tag, pushes `master` and the tag, and opens a GitHub Release whose body is that changelog
section. A version that already shipped fails on its existing tag instead of being moved.

Notes are written for users: what changed, and what to do about it when upgrading.
